Package org.apache.poi.ss.util

Class ExcelArithmetic

java.lang.Object
org.apache.poi.ss.util.ExcelArithmetic
public final class ExcelArithmetic extends Object
Arithmetic helpers that reproduce how Excel computes with IEEE 754 doubles.

Excel stores and calculates in double precision, but only ever exposes 15 significant decimal digits, and it compensates for binary representation error in a few well-defined places. These helpers implement those places so that formula evaluation matches what a user sees in Excel.

Since:
6.0.0
See Also:
  • Floating-point arithmetic may give inaccurate result in Excel

  • Method Details

    • approxValue

      public static double approxValue(double d)
      Returns the value as Excel sees it: rounded to 15 significant decimal digits. Functions that truncate (INT, FLOOR, CEILING, MOD, ...) act on this view rather than on the raw binary value - e.g. INT(2490399.9999999995) is 2490400 in Excel. Integers and values with few fractional bits are exactly representable and are returned unchanged.

    • toBigDecimal

      public static BigDecimal toBigDecimal(double d)
      Returns the value as Excel sees it, as an exact decimal: the 15 significant digits of approxValue(double), so that decimal arithmetic on it (rounding to a number of places, or to a multiple of a step) gives the answer Excel gives. 0.1*3 is 0.3 rather than 0.30000000000000004, and 2.675 is exactly that rather than 2.67499999999999982236431605997495353221893310546875.
      Parameters:
      d - a finite double
      Throws:
      NumberFormatException - if d is NaN or infinite
      Since:
      6.0.0

      Returns:
